simple.meaning: כָּנָף (kânâph) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “an edge or extremity ; specifically (of a bird or army) a wing , (of a garment or bedclothing) a flap , (of the earth) a quarter , (of a building) a pinnacle.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 111 times across Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, and 12 more, beginning at Genesis 1:21. Its contexts include offering, altar, priesthood, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כָּנָף (H3671).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: כָּנָף (kânâph) / H3671 is traced through Genesis 1:21, Genesis 7:14, Exodus 19:4, Exodus 25:20 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H3671. kanaph כָּנָף 109 noun feminine 1Kin 6:27 ( masculine Ezek 7:2 Kt, but compare Qr and Co; also apparently 2Chr 3:11 , 13 , but see Be), wing, extremity (Late Hebrew id. ; Aramaic כַּנְפָֿא , ; Zinjirli מראה בכנף אחז , figurative for attached himself to the party of his lord , Panammu Inscr. l. 11, compare Zech 8:23 ( 2a below); DHM Sendsch. 58 ; Arabic , Assyrian kappu , Ethiopic ); — absolute ׳כ Gen 1:21 +; construct כְּנַף 1Kin 6:24 +; suffix כְּנָפִי Ezek 16:8 , כְּנָפֶ֑ךָ Ruth 3:9 , כְּנָפוֺ Hag 2:12 ; dual כְּנָפַיִם 1Kin 8:7 + (even of more than two, Isa 6:2 (twice in verse); Ezek 1:6 , 21 ); construct כַּנְפֵי Exod 19:4 ; suffix כְּנָפֶיךָ Ezek 5:3 , כְּנָפַיִךְ Jer 2:34 , כְּנָפָיו Isa 8:8 +; כְּנָפֶיהָ Hosea 4:19 ; Malachi 3:20; כַּנְפֵיהֶם 1Kin 6:27 +; כַנְפֵיהֶן Ezek 1:24-25 , plural construct כַּנְפוֺת Deut 22:12 4 t.; — 1 wing , a. of birds Isa 10:14 (in figurative), Exod 19:4 (E ? R ? figurative) Deut 32:11 (in simile), Zech 5:9 ; Lev 1:17 (P), Job 39:13 , 26 ; Psa 68:14 ; in figure of invading king Jer 48:40 ; 49:22 ; Ezek 17:3 , 7 ; so apparently Isa 8:8 of invader as overflowing river (but Du Che separate כְּנָפָיו מֻטּוֺת וְהָיָה from preceding); of riches, as flying away Prov 23:5 ; in phrase כָּנָף צִמּוֺר = winged birds Deut 4:17 ; Psa 148:10 , כָּלכֿ ׳(עֵיט)צִמּוֺר Ezek 39:4 , 17 , כָּלכֿ צִמּוֺר ׳כֹּל Gen 7:14 (P), Ezek 17:23 , כ ׳עוֺף Gen 1:21 (P), Psa 78:27 ; also כ ׳בַּעַל Prov 1:17 = winged thing , compare בַּעַלהֿ֯כְּנָפַיִם Eccl 10:20 . b. of insects (probably), כְּנָפָ֑יִם צִלְצַל אֶרֶץ Isa 18:1 buzzing , or humming of wings , i.e. Ethiopia, so called from its swarms of flies, with especial reference possibly to the tsetse-fly (so Du, compare Che; id., in General, Hi De; > Kn Di of the tropical shadow falling both ways ; Thes 1167b of noise of the wings of an army; reference to sails as wings — compare 18:2 — would be suitable, but צִלְצַל does not favour this). c. of cherubim 1Kin 6:24 (4 t. in verse) + 8 t. Kings, compare 2Chr 3:11 (4 t. in verse) + 6 t. Chronicles; Ezek 1:6 17 t. Ezekiel; Exod 25:20 (twice in verse); 39:9 (twice in verse) (all P). d. of seraphim Isa 6:2 (twice in verse). e. of women in Zechariah's vision Zech 5:9 (twice in verse). f. figurative of the wind, Hosea 4:19 ; Psa 18:11 = 2Sam 22:11 ; Psa 104:3 . g. figurative of the dawn (winged sun-disc ?) Psa 139:9 , compare of sun of righteousness Malachi 3:20. h. figurative of ׳י , as protector of his people Psa 17:8 ; 36:8 ; 57:2 ; 61:5 ; 63:3 ; 91:4 ; Ruth 2:12 . 2 extremity: — a. of garment = skirt, corner , or loose flowing end, 1Sam 15:27 ; 24:5 ; 24:6 ; 24:12 (twice in verse); Deut 22:12 ; 23:1 ; 27:20 ; Jer 2:34 (figurative), Ezek 5:3 ; 16:8 (in figurative), Hag 2:12 (twice in verse); Zech 8:23 ; Num 15:38 (twice in verse) (P; compare RS Sem, i. 416, 2nd ed. 437 ). b. of the earth , הָאָרֶץ מִכְּנַף Isa 24:16 from the end of the earth ; elsewhere plural הָא ׳כַּנְפוֺת Job 37:3 ; 38:13 , and, def. כ ׳אַרְבַּע ׳הא Isa 11:12 the four corners of the earth ; so of the holy land Ezek 7:2 . — מְשׁוֺמֵם שִׁקּוּצִים עַלכְּֿנַף Dan 9:27 is obscure; Meinh reads, after Vrss., כָּנָף , on the corner (of the altar) is a devastating abomination ; < Kue Onderzoek 2, ii. 472 Bev, who read עַלכַּֿנּוֺ in its place, instead of it.
